parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two identical oil droplets are in a vacuum. The centres of the droplets are a distance of 3.8 × 10⁻⁶ m apart. The droplets have equal charge and exert an electric force on each other of magnitude 6.3 × 10⁻¹⁷ N.

Determine the magnitude of the charge on each droplet.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
One of the oil droplets in (b) is now placed between two horizontal metal plates, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

A potential difference (p.d.) of 120 V is applied between the plates, with the top plate at the higher potential. The oil droplet is stationary and in equilibrium.
parts.text: State the sign of the charge on the oil droplet.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, draw four lines to represent the electric field between the plates.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The distance between the plates is 5.2 cm.

Determine the mass of the oil droplet.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A labelled oil droplet is between two horizontal metal plates, with a 120 V connection to the upper plate, a 0 V connection to the lower plate, and the plate separation marked as 5.2 cm.
